GitHub-Runner gets a web interface. Everything that used to live in environment variables can now be watched and changed on port 8080, and an existing install keeps working as it is.

## ✨ Added

- A web interface on port 8080. Each repository is a line: waiting for jobs, running one, restarting or refused. The jobs of the last two hours sit on it as stops, a running job shows how far it is compared with its usual length, and every repository has its live log and its last jobs.
- Add a repository by name, as `owner/name`, as a GitHub link or by its name alone with a default owner. GitHub is asked first, so a token that is rejected (401), lacks the rights (403) or cannot see the repository (404) is named right there, and nothing is added.
- Remove a repository, restart its runner or try a refused one again at once. Removing takes the runner off GitHub too.
- Labels per repository, next to the labels all runners share.
- Every setting from the environment variables in the settings: token, default owner, runner name, labels, the default labels, root or not, cleanup on stop and the retry time. A new token makes every refused repository try again right away.
- An optional password. Nothing is locked until you set one, under any address. Only a hash is stored, the session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, requests from other sites are refused, and wrong tries are answered more slowly while the right password always gets through.
- **Forgot password?** on the sign-in page writes a code to the container log. It is valid for 10 minutes, and with it you set a new password, which ends every other session.
- The settings live in `/config/config.json`, the job history of the last two days next to it, so the lines survive a restart. The first start fills the file from the environment variables you already have.
- Light and dark, following your device or picked by hand, and motion that stays still when your system asks for less.

## ⚡ Improved

- A missing token or an empty repository list no longer stops the container. It waits with one line in the log that says what is missing, so you can fill it in on the web interface.
- A new `ACCESS_TOKEN` in the container settings replaces the saved token at the next start. Repositories that are new in `RUNNER_REPOS` are added at the next start, and one taken out of the list keeps its runner until you remove it in the web interface. The other variables only fill the settings on the first start, and the log says so when one of them changes later.
- The health check asks the service itself, which knows whether every runner is listening and also notices when the service hangs.
- A Go service runs the runners in place of the shell script, with the same log lines as before. Stopping removes the registrations in parallel, so many repositories fit into the minute the container gets to stop.
- The build runs the Go and web interface tests first, and the smoke test now also checks the web interface and adds and removes a repository through it with a real token.
